items.note: PDF read via curl/pypdf. States the council on 11.12. committed to becoming climate-neutral 'alsbald - möglichst bis 2030', climate budget 'erheblich angehoben' (to >10 M EUR for 2020-2023); commentary calls the goal 'eine rechtlich unverbindliche Absichtserklärung'. Note: this is the newsletter of the Klima-Initiative Münster (a citizens' group), hosted on the city site, not a city publication. Title 'MS Klimainfo 2020 01' is only the file name.

V/0552/2024 p.3-4: since 2020 payment at Parkscheinautomaten also by smartphone; framework contract with smartparking; seven apps listed; traditional machines remain in operation. Title and wording match.

V/0830/2021 (Beschlussvorlage dated 16.11.2021, decision by Hauptausschuss 15.12.2021): transfer of operation of Radstation with over 2,000 spaces in Hansator (Bremer Platz 50) to WBI, operation to start 01.07.2022; refers to a 'möglichen Inbetriebnahme eines weiteren Fahrradparkhauses im umgebauten Parkhaus Bremer Platz in 2025' and '2. Stufe des Projektes Mobility-Hub Parkhaus Bremer Platz'. Text correctly keeps it a proposal/possibility.
Anlage A to V/0194/2022: the proposal adapts on-street meter fees to the 'zum 1. Januar 2022 erfolgte Erhöhung der Parkentgelte' in WBI garages in the city.

Page: 'Im Dezember 2022 beschloss der Rat ..., die beiden Parkplätze im Bereich des Domplatzes aufzugeben'; since October 2023 the former car park on the west side is newly used with benches, tables and loungers for sitting, relaxing.

FAQ page states the council adopted a new fee ordinance for resident permits on 13 December 2023 and a permit 'derzeit' costs 260 EUR per year. It does NOT mention February 2024; that start date comes from a different document (V/0552/2024), not this source.
items.corrected_text: The council adopted a new fee ordinance for residents' parking permits on 13 December 2023; a permit currently costs 260 euros a year.

items.note: V/0552/2024 confirms the council on 19.06.2024 adopted the Integrated Parking Concept 'mehrheitlich geändert', covering the city centre, station area and nearby quarters, with new residents' parking zones as an essential element. The claim that the city described the aim as making street parking dearer than garage parking is not in this report (it is in the 10 Dec 2025 city release, item 12).
items.corrected_text: On 19 June 2024 the council adopted, with amendments, an Integrated Parking Concept covering the city centre, the station area and nearby districts; introducing new residents' parking zones is a core element.

items.note: ms-aktuell (3 Dec 2024): proposal presented at the latest WBI supervisory board meeting; from 1 Sept 2025 prices 'könnten' rise; central garages such as Aegidiimarkt, Theater, Münster-Arkaden first hour 2.50 -> 3.00 EUR; 'Die Entscheidung ist noch nicht gefallen'. Text correctly keeps it a plan. However, the final clause about the December 2025 city release is not on this page (it is accurate per the 10 Dec 2025 release, item 12, which lists first hour 'bisher 2,50 Euro'), so it should be cited to that source or dropped.
items.corrected_text: A local news site reported that a proposal presented to WBI's supervisory board could raise prices in central garages such as Aegidiimarkt, Theater and Münster-Arkaden from September 2025, with the first hour going from 2.50 to 3.00 euros. It said no decision had yet been taken.

items.note: City release dated 11.03.2025: garage with 'fast 1000' spaces opens as P+R on all Saturdays, first date Saturday 22 March; tested 'zunächst für zwei Jahre'; 5-euro day ticket, up to five people ride city buses to the centre; previously only on Advent Saturdays. Release is an announcement before the start, but the 12.08.2025 release (item 11) refers to Saturday P+R there 'wie gewohnt'.
Release 07.05.2025: new web presence covering 19 Parkhäuser; free spaces and open/closed shown, updates every minute; click shows prices, opening hours, clearance heights and EV charging options.

Release 16.05.2025 says private providers installed about 50 new charging STATIONS (Ladesäulen, not points) in recent weeks in public space under a city tender (examples Ludgeriplatz, Turmstraße, Rjasanstraße, Sentruper Straße); about 50 more by end of June; BEV registrations up almost 19% (early 2024 to early 2025) to 7,122. 'Mostly at street locations' is an inference; the page says public space with street examples. No mention of WBI or garages (correct).
items.corrected_text: Private operators installed about 50 new public charging stations in public space in recent weeks under a city tender, for example at Ludgeriplatz and Turmstraße, with about 50 more due by the end of June 2025. Registered battery-electric cars in Münster rose almost 19% between early 2024 and early 2025 to 7,122; the release does not mention garages.

items.note: Release 12.08.2025: festival 15-17 August; Klemensstraße, Prinzipalmarkt and Drubbel (to Neubrückenstraße) closed from Thu 14 Aug 14:00 to Mon 18 Aug 05:00; municipal garages normal hours; Coesfelder Kreuz P+R on the Saturday. (The release itself writes 'Samstag, 15. August', although 15 Aug 2025 was a Friday; the draft's 'on the Saturday' avoids the error.)

Release 10.12.2025 confirms council decision on 10 Dec, effective 1 Jan 2026, zone I extended to the station area, WBI garages first hour 2.50 -> 3.00 and each further hour 2.00 -> 2.50, exclusions Coesfelder Kreuz/Stadthaus 3/Cineplex, previous increase 1 May 2022. But zone I 2.50 -> 3.50 is the FIRST-HOUR rate (previously 2.50 first hour + 1.00 per further 30 min; now 3.50 first hour + 1.50 per further 30 min), not a flat 'hourly rate'.
items.corrected_text: On 10 December 2025 the council approved higher parking charges from 1 January 2026, extending central zone I to the station area: there the first hour rises from 2.50 to 3.50 euros and each further half hour from 1.00 to 1.50 euros. In WBI garages the first hour rises from 2.50 to 3.00 euros and each further hour from 2.00 to 2.50 euros (excluding Coesfelder Kreuz, Stadthaus 3 and Cineplex); the previous increase was on 1 May 2022.

items.note: ms-aktuell (21 Dec 2025; headline matches, HTML <title> differs). Counts correct: ~85,000 each on Prinzipalmarkt and Ludgeristraße on the first Advent weekend; mid-December Saturday Ludgeristraße ~88,000, Prinzipalmarkt ~80,000. But the article says only the new laser counter on Prinzipalmarkt was installed by hystreet with Wirtschaftsförderung Münster (since Advent); it does not say counters on both streets were newly installed.
items.corrected_text: A new laser pedestrian counter on Prinzipalmarkt, installed by hystreet with Münster's economic development agency, began counting in Advent 2025. First figures showed about 85,000 passers-by each on Prinzipalmarkt and Ludgeristraße on the first Advent weekend, and about 88,000 on Ludgeristraße and 80,000 on Prinzipalmarkt on a busy mid-December Saturday.

items.note: ms-aktuell 19 Feb 2026 (URL redirects to slug 'oepnv-mit-millionenpublikum...' but headline matches): per Stadtwerke, 31.9 million bus passengers last year; subscriptions rose to more than 60,000; 'Vor allem das Deutschlandticket sorgte für einen deutlichen Zuwachs'.

ms-aktuell 13 Mar 2026: a political initiative (Antrag) before the Münster-Mitte district council; street parking in many Altstadt streets to remain only in exceptional cases (mobility-impaired, deliveries, care/service); streets named incl. Königsstraße, Alter Steinweg, Drubbel, Roggenmarkt, Bogenstraße, Spiekerhof. Access restriction is hedged: in several streets traffic 'könnte' be limited mainly to Anlieger (local access) and delivery traffic, steering traffic to existing garages. Draft generalises the access limit and says 'residents' only.
items.corrected_text: A proposal before the Münster-Mitte district council in March 2026 sought to sharply reduce street parking in Altstadt streets such as Königsstraße, Alter Steinweg, Drubbel and Spiekerhof, keeping spaces mainly for people with reduced mobility and deliveries. In several streets traffic could be limited mainly to local-access and delivery traffic, steering drivers to existing garages; it was a proposal, not a decision.

items.note: ms-aktuell article dated 18 Apr 2026 (before the works), written as an announcement 'nach den vorliegenden Informationen': WBI starts conversion in April at Parkhaus Bahnhofstraße, closed 20-24 April; in future licence-plate recognition 'an vielen Standorten'; cashless payment, lighting, stairwells planned there; WBI runs eight city-centre garages with ~3,900 spaces. The draft states as completed fact that work started and the garage was closed; the page does not confirm this happened.
items.corrected_text: A local news site reported that WBI, which runs eight city-centre garages with about 3,900 spaces, was starting to convert its garages from paper tickets to licence-plate recognition, beginning with the Bahnhofstraße garage, which was to close 20-24 April 2026. Cashless payment and new lighting and stairwells were also planned there.

corrected_summary: Münster's council set a goal in December 2019 to become climate-neutral, ideally by 2030, and in June 2024 adopted an Integrated Parking Concept which the city says aims to make street parking dearer than garage parking; the council decided in December 2022 to give up the Domplatz parking areas, and a March 2026 district-council proposal sought to cut street parking in Altstadt streets. WBI raised garage charges in January 2022, and the council approved higher on-street and WBI garage fees from January 2026; in April 2026 a local news site reported WBI was starting to convert garages to licence-plate entry. Other context includes Saturday park-and-ride at Coesfelder Kreuz from March 2025, a new Parkleitsystem website in May 2025, and more than 60,000 public transport subscriptions, with the Deutschlandticket cited as the main source of growth.
